title: Open Policy Agent - Homepage
snippet: Open Policy Agent (OPA) is an open-source policy engine that evaluates authorization decisions using Rego policies decoupled from application code. OPA was accepted into the CNCF on March 29, 2018, moved to incubating on April 2, 2019, and reached graduated status on January 29, 2021.
claim: OPA achieved CNCF graduated status in 2021 as the standard policy-as-code engine

snippet: Rego is a declarative policy language designed to evaluate structured data such as JSON inputs and return structured decisions. Rego was inspired by Datalog and extends it to support structured document models such as JSON.

topic: Cedar as AWS-focused authorization engine with safety-by-default design
query: Cedar policy engine AWS Amazon Rego OPA comparison
title: Comparing OPA/Rego to AWS Cedar and Google Zanzibar - Styra
snippet: Cedar is focused on application-level authorization and is more readable than Rego. Cedar is more strict and structured with emphasis on safety by default (deny by default), and more assurances on correctness/security thanks to verification-guided development.
claim: Cedar provides safety-by-default authorization with stricter semantics than Rego

topic: OPA flexibility for multi-use policy vs Cedar domain-specific authorization focus

title: Policy as Code: OPA's Rego vs. Cedar
snippet: OPA/Rego stand out due to their flexibility, expressiveness, and extensibility for policy enforcement across network, infrastructure, and applications. Cedar is designed around the PARC model for application-level authorization decisions.
claim: OPA/Rego support general-purpose policy across layers; Cedar specializes in application authorization
